heroHeadline: BILD, TELEGRAPH DETAIL RUSSIA-NATO ATTACK SCENARIOS; BALTIC, NORDIC LEADERS PUSH BACK (AUG 31); TRUMP SAYS RUSSIA 'NOT GOING TO ATTACK' AS BLOOMBERG REPORTS ALLIES SKEPTICAL OF RATCLIFFE'S MOSCOW TRIP (AUG 28); COLBY BRIEFS ALL 32 AMBASSADORS ON FORCE POSTURE REVIEW (AUG 27)
heroSubtitle: As of August 31, 2026, the NATO-US tracker's dominant story remains the credibility of Article 5 deterrence amid the Pentagon's Europe force-posture review. German tabloid Bild and the UK's Telegraph reported August 31 detailed scenarios for how Russia could test NATO short of a full invasion — from unrest in Estonia's Narva to a Suwałki Corridor push to Article 5-testing cyberattacks — prompting pushback from Baltic and Nordic leaders including Latvia's PM Kulbergs, Finland's President Stubb, Estonia's FM Tsahkna and Romania's Defence Minister Miruță, all of whom said they see no evidence of an imminent conventional attack even as Russian hybrid activity continues. That followed a Bloomberg report on August 28 that European officials are skeptical CIA Director John Ratcliffe's August 25 Moscow visit was mainly meant to deter a Baltic attack, with President Trump telling reporters Russia is 'not going to attack.' The same day, the Daily Caller, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported Defense Secretary Hegseth drafted a further troop-reduction plan in June but scrapped it after Secretary of State Marco Rubio intervened — the first concrete sign of an internal administration split over the posture review's scope. That followed US Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby's August 27 briefing of all 32 NATO ambassadors in Brussels, where he confirmed the controversial allied loyalty questionnaire was sent deliberately 'in the spirit of NATO 3.0,' with the review now centered on base access and overflight rather than a blunt troop-drawdown target; Reuters separately reported the review will yield four sets of troop-level options for Hegseth by November 6, with allies having faced an August 29 deadline to submit written questionnaire responses.
